title: Tunisian lace stitch wrap
excerpt: A lightweight rectangular wrap worked in Tunisian lace stitch using fingering yarn. The open mesh creates a delicate drape ideal for layering over shoulders.
sourceNotes: Tunisian lace stitch combines yarn-overs with Tunisian simple stitch pick-ups to create an open fabric on a long Tunisian hook.

glossaryTerms.definition: A stitch that pairs a yarn-over with a skip on the forward pass to create an open eyelet row within the Tunisian fabric.
Wrapping yarn over the hook before picking up the next vertical bar. The loop sits on the hook and pairs with a skip to form an eyelet.
The base Tunisian stitch: insert hook through the front vertical bar and draw up a loop, leaving it on the hook until the return pass.

crochet.gaugeText: 18 sts x 14 rows = 10 cm in Tunisian lace stitch on 3.5 mm hook.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Approx. 45 cm wide x 140 cm long.

Chain 82. Forward pass row 1: pick up a loop in the 2nd chain from hook and in each chain across (82 loops on hook). Return pass: chain 1, then work off 2 loops at a time to end.
Forward pass: pick up the first vertical bar, then *yarn over, skip 1 bar, pick up next bar; repeat from * across. Return pass: ch 1, work off 2 loops to end. Repeat these 2 rows throughout.
Continue the lace repeat until the wrap measures 140 cm. Bind off with a slip stitch across all bars: insert hook through bar, yarn over, pull through both loops.
Weave in the ends with the tapestry needle. Block flat by pinning to measurements and misting with water, then leave to dry.
